name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to a Defect in Testosterone Metabolism by Peripheral Tissue
aliases: 46,XY DSD due to peripheral testosterone metabolism defect
Peripheral androgen metabolism disorder in 46,XY individuals

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous genitalia or undervirilization in a 46,XY individual
Abnormal peripheral testosterone metabolism evidenced by altered ratios of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone or other androgen metabolites
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes involved in peripheral testosterone metabolism (e.g., 5-alpha reductase deficiency)
Imaging showing presence of internal male reproductive structures with ambiguous external genitalia
Positive family history of similar DSD or androgen metabolism defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY individual plus abnormal hormonal profile and confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and radiology.

searchTerms: ambiguous external sex organs with micropenis

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal urethral opening along the ventral penile shaft
Delayed or incomplete development of secondary male sexual characteristics

common.notes: Testes may be undescended or ectopic
Breast tissue development due to androgen deficiency
searchTerms: breast tissue growth in teenage boys

common.notes: Impaired spermatogenesis due to androgen deficiency

occasional.notes: Skeletal maturation lagging behind chronological age

searchTerms: small male breast growth in childhood

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
occasional.notes: Emotional and social challenges due to atypical genitalia
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia

occasional.notes: Lower than expected muscle bulk for age and sex

searchTerms: high blood pressure from hormone imbalance

rare.notes: Reported in isolated cases, unclear association
Uncommon and not directly linked to primary defect

laboratory: Abnormal androgen metabolite profiles in urine
Normal or elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence of testes and internal male reproductive structures
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SRD5A2 gene (5-alpha reductase type 2 deficiency)
Mutations in genes affecting peripheral androgen metabolism enzymes
other: Histological examination of gonadal tissue confirming testicular tissue
Psychosocial assessment for gender identity and support needs

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated testosterone with absent or minimal androgen receptor function
Defect in testosterone biosynthesis rather than peripheral metabolism
Low serum testosterone with elevated androstenedione
Similar undervirilization but different enzymatic defect

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Failure to virilize during puberty in a 46,XY individual
Family history of similar disorders or consanguinity
references: Hughes IA et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Maimoun L, Philibert P, Cammas B, et al. Peripheral androgen metabolism defects in 46,XY DSD. Endocr Rev. 2011.
Orphanet: 46,XY difference of sex development due to a defect in testosterone metabolism by peripheral tissue. ORPHA:98086.
